§ 2Content

Order of Advent of Europeans in India

  1. 1. Portuguese (1498)
  2. 2. Dutch (1602)
  3. 3. English (1608)
  4. 4. Danes (1616)
  5. 5. French (1668)

§ 3PORTUGUESE

Arrival of Portuguese

  • The Portuguese came to India for various economic and religious reasons. They were the first to introduce tobacco and cashew nuts in India. They were also the first to come and last to go.
Treaty of Tordesillas, signed on 7th June 1494 was a significant agreement between Spain and Portugal. It aimed to resolve conflicts over newly discovered lands by dividing the world into two spheres of influence. The treaty established a demarcation line, with lands to the east belonging to Portugal and lands to the west to Spain.

Vasco da Gama (1498)

  • He was also the first to discover the sea route to India.
  • He was a Portuguese explorer who came to Calicut during the rule of King Zamorin (then Hindu ruler of Calicut).

Francisco de Almeida (1505)

  • He was the first Portuguese Viceroy of India.
  • He brought "Blue Water Policy" (Cartaz System) which was a trade licensing system that allowed the Portuguese to control trade in Indian Ocean.

Afonso de Albuquerque (1509)

  • He was the second Portuguese Governor of India.
  • He captured Goa in 1510 and abolished Sati.

Nuno da Cunha

  • He was a Portuguese Governor who moved capital from Cochin to Goa in 1530.
Bahadur Shah, ruler of Gujarat surrendered Diu to Portuguese in 1535.

§ 4DUTCH

Arrival of Dutch

  • Dutch refers to "people from Netherlands".
  • Dutch East India Company was formed in 1602.
  • They set up their first factory in Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) in Andhra Pradesh in 1605.

§ 5ENGLISH

Arrival of English

  • 1599: East India Company came into existence.
  • 1600: East India Company received a Royal Charter from Queen Elizabeth I to trade in India.
  • 1608: William Hawkins arrived in the court of Jahangir.
  • 1611: First factory at Masulipatnam (temporary).
  • 1613: First factory at Surat (permanent).
  • 1615: Sir Thomas Roe visited Jahangir's court to receive the trading rights.
  • 1620: Danes established their first factory at Tranquebar (Tamil Nadu).
  • 1668: French established their first factory at Surat.

§ 6EXPANSION OF BRITISHERS

  • Battle of Chiusurah/Bedara/Hooghly in 1759 that took place on the banks of Hooghly river in which Britishers defeated the Dutch.
  • Battle of Swally/Suwali in Surat in 1612 in which the Britishers defeated the Portuguese.
Battle of Colachel in 1741 between Marthanda Varma (King of Travancore) and Dutch East India Company.

§ 7CARNATIC WARS

  • The series of Carnatic Wars started between British and French East India Companies.
  • A total of 3 Carnatic Wars were fought between 1744 and 1763.
  • Dupleix led the French forces in the first two Carnatic Wars.

1st Carnatic War (1744-1748)

  • It ended with Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle.
  • Won by: French East India Company.

2nd Carnatic War (1749-1754)

  • It started with Battle of Ambur (won by British) and ended with Treaty of Pondicherry.

3rd Carnatic War (1756-1763)

  • Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was a part of 3rd Carnatic War.
  • This war was an extension of Anglo-French War of 7 years which were caused by Austrian War of Succession.
  • It ended with Treaty of Paris.
  • British forces led by Sir Eyre Coote defeated the French forces led by Comte de Lally.

§ 8IN BENGAL

  • 1717-1727: Murshid Quli Khan served as the first Nawab of Bengal.
  • In 1717, Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar issued a Golden Farman (Magna Carta of Trade) that allowed the British East India Company to trade freely in Bengal for a yearly payment of 3,000 Rupees. The farman also granted the company the right to issue Dastaks, or trade permits, to move goods.

Nawabs of Bengal

Murshid Quli Khan → Shuja-ud-Din Muhammad Khan → Alivardi Khan (died in 1756) → Siraj-ud-Daulah

Siraj-ud-Daulah

  • He became the Nawab at the age of 23 years after the death of Alivardi Khan in 1756.
  • He was the last self-governing Nawab of Bengal.
  • He was not happy with the Trade privileges enjoyed by Britishers in Bengal.
  • Siraj-ud-Daulah, captured the Fort William after the British refused to stop fortifying it. The Black Hole Tragedy was a night of captivity for British soldiers and other prisoners in a small, airless room in Fort William, Calcutta in 1756. This incident instigated Robert Clive, who decided to take revenge, which led to the Battle of Plassey.

Battle of Plassey (1757)

  • It was fought between the East India Company force led by Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Bengal).
  • Mir Jafar, the military commander of Siraj-ud-Daulah joined hands with the Britishers.
  • This battle confirmed the formal beginning of British Empire in India.
Treaty of Alinagar (1757) was signed between Siraj-ud-Daulah and the Britishers which became the cause of Battle of Plassey.

Outcomes of Battle of Plassey

  • Siraj-ud-Daulah fled the battlefield and was captured afterwards. He was executed on 2 July 1757 by Mohammad Ali Beg under orders of Mir Miran (son of Mir Jafar). Note: Mir Madan, Siraj's general, was killed in the Battle of Plassey itself.
  • Mir Jafar was made the new puppet Nawab of Bengal.
  • Then Mughal Emperor: Alamgir II.
  • Subsequently, Mir Qasim (son-in-law of Mir Jafar) came to the throne. He shifted the capital from Murshidabad to Munger (he also ended Dastak issued by Farrukhsiyar).
  • Combined forces of Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh), Mir Qasim and Shah Alam II (Mughal Emperor) led to Battle of Buxar (1764) against the Britishers.
  • 1st Nawab of Awadh: Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk.
  • The fourth Nawab of Awadh → Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula, built Bara Imambara in Lucknow.

Battle of Buxar (1764)

  • Britishers won this battle led by Hector Munro.
  • Treaty of Allahabad was signed in 1765 between Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II and Robert Clive (then Governor). Under this, two separate treaty were signed.

First Treaty with Nawab of Awadh:

  • Allahabad and Kara were handed over to Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.
  • Nawab paid Rs 50 lakh to the British as war indemnity.

Second Treaty with Shah Alam II:

  • Emperor Shah Alam II was placed under British protection at Allahabad.
  • Diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa were given to the East India Company, in return of an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
  • The Company was to receive Rs 53 lakh from the Emperor for performing nizamat (military and judicial) functions in these provinces. This control over Diwani and Nizamat Functions by East India Company is called as Dual Government in Bengal.
  • Mir Jafar was made the Nawab again.
  • Allahabad Treaty ran for 7 years and was ended by Warren Hastings in 1772.

§ 9IN MYSORE

  • In Mysore, Wodeyar Dynasty was ruling. Hyder Ali who was a soldier under Wodeyar Dynasty and ultimately sat on the throne of Mysore.

Anglo-Mysore Wars

#### 1st Anglo-Mysore War (1767-1769)

  • It ended with the Treaty of Madras.
  • Won by: Mysore.

#### 2nd Anglo-Mysore War (1780-1784)

  • Hyder Ali was defeated in the Battle of Porto Novo (1781) by the British forces led by Sir Eyre Coote.
  • Tipu Sultan sat on throne after the death of his father Hyder Ali due to cancer in the middle of the war.
  • It ended with Treaty of Mangalore.

#### 3rd Anglo-Mysore War (1790-1792)

  • It ended with Treaty of Seringapatnam.
  • 3rd Mysore War led to defeat of Tipu Sultan (Capital: Seringapatnam) with heavy fine imposed on him and his two sons were captured as hostages.

#### 4th Anglo-Mysore War (1798-1799)

  • Due to growing proximity of Tipu Sultan with French, Britishers waged another war with him.
  • Tipu Sultan was killed in the Battle.

Subsidiary Alliance

  • Subsidiary alliance was introduced by Lord Wellesley in 1798, though it was a brain-child of French Governor General Lord Dupleix.
  • Under the subsidiary alliance, Indian rulers had to pay subsidy for the British Garrison and British Army deployed in their territory. They had to seek permission from British EIC to partner with any other European for any service, and also for the negotiations with other Indian rulers.
  • Adopted by: Hyderabad (first State to sign in 1798) & Mysore (in 1799); Tanjore (in 1799); Awadh (in 1801) and Peshwa (in 1802).

§ 10IN PUNJAB

  • Maharaja Ranjit Singh from Sukerchakia Misl (one of the 12 Sikh Misls) signed Treaty of Amritsar in 1809 with British and declared Sutlej river as boundary between the Sikh Kingdom and the British Empire.
  • He died in 1839.

Anglo-Sikh Wars

#### 1st Anglo-Sikh War (1845)

  • It resulted in the defeat and partial subjugation of the Sikh Empire and cession of Jammu & Kashmir as a separate princely state under British suzerainty.
Battle of Aliwal (1846) — It was a part of 1st Anglo-Sikh War.
  • Treaty of Lahore (Lahore was the capital) and Treaty of Bhairowal were signed between Maharaja Duleep Singh and British.

#### 2nd Anglo-Sikh War (1848)

  • Maharaja Duleep Singh was captured and Kohinoor diamond was stolen. Lord Dalhousie was then Governor-General of India.

§ 11AFGHANS

#### 1st Anglo-Afghan War (1839-1842)

  • Dost Muhammad Khan, the Afghan ruler was dethroned and Shah Shuja was placed on the throne.
  • 1st Anglo-Afghan War took place during the tenure of Lord Auckland (Governor-General of India).
  • John Lawrence (Governor-General) implemented Policy of Masterly Inactivity towards Afghan Empire during his tenure.

#### 2nd Anglo-Afghan War (1878-1880)

  • Treaty of Gandamak signed (Lord Lytton was the Viceroy)

#### 3rd Anglo-Afghan War (1919)

§ 12BURMA (Myanmar)

#### 1st Anglo Burma War (1824-1826)

  • It ended with the Treaty of Yandaboo (1826).

#### 2nd Anglo Burma War (1852-1853)
